course_description:
This pharmaceutical science course explores drug delivery systems that involve the active pharmaceutical ingredient being in a solid form, such as tablets and capsules, or a semi-solid form, such as creams, ointments and gels. It also considers the design of devices that deliver medicines via the transdermal route, such as patches, and devices for pulmonary or buccal delivery, such as inhalers, vaping devices and mouth sprays. Students then gain experience in extemporaneous compounding of solid and semi-solid medicines, including creams, ointments, pastes, capsules and suppositories.

Pharmacists must understand the physicochemical basis of drug formulation and drug delivery systems to extemporaneously compounded medicines, select the appropriate dosage form to be administered (or suggest alternatives) and predict the behaviour and efficacy of pharmaceuticals. There is a strong emphasis on active learning, data analysis, and calculations throughout this course, which is divided into the four modules described below.

Module 1 Solid Dosage Forms introduces the wide range of solid dosage forms, such as tablets, capsules, lozenges, gums, pessaries and suppositories. You will examine powder characteristics such as particle properties and powder flow, and pharmaceutical concepts encompassing dissolution and bioavailability. Manufacturing processes along with quality assurance and quality control will be covered, and you will measure tablet properties such as uniformity, hardness, friability, disintegration and dissolution in the laboratory. Module 1 is assessed by an online quiz and the end of semester exam.

Module 2 Semi-Solid Dosage Forms explores the physicochemical basis for designing different types of semi-solids such as creams, gels, ointments and pastes. You will consider rheological properties of pharmaceutical products, and in the laboratory you will investigate these characteristics for polymer-based formulations with the aim of understanding product design, formulation and effective use. Module 2 is assessed by an online quiz and the end of semester exam.

Module 3 Specialised Devices considers devices designed for delivery of medicines via the transdermal route, such as patches, and devices for pulmonary or buccal delivery such as inhalers, vaping devices and mouth sprays. You will explore the mechanism by which they deliver medicines in the context of their practical applications. Module 3 is assessed by an online quiz and the end of semester exam.

Module 4 Compounding Semi-Solid and Solid Dosage Forms focuses on extemporaneous compounding and is taught primarily through weekly in-person practical classes, where you will gain experience preparing pharmaceutically elegant dosage forms such as capsules, suppositories, creams, ointments, and pastes. You will practice pharmaceutical calculations relevant to semi-solid and liquid dosage forms throughout the course, and especially during Module 4. Module 4 is assessed by an in-person calculations quiz and a practical compounding skills assessment. The compounding skills assessment is a hurdle to pass this course.

course_aims: This course will contribute to your formation as a pharmacist who understands the physicochemical basis of the formulation and clinical use of medicines. You will learn to explain and apply physicochemical principles to the formulation of medicines into solid and semi-solid dosage forms, and specialised devices for transdermal, pulmonary, and buccal delivery. You will also develop skills in the extemporaneous compounding of solid and semi-solid medicines, including creams, ointments, pastes, capsules, and suppositories.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply physicochemical principles to the formulation of semi-solid and solid dosage forms and medicines use.
Explain the mechanism of transdermal, pulmonary, and buccal delivery through specialised devices to inform medicines use.
Collate, analyse, and interpret scientific data to inform pharmaceutical decisions.
Perform pharmaceutical calculations relating to semi-solid and solid medicines.
Design and prepare accurate and pharmaceutically elegant extemporaneous semi-solid and solid dosage forms.

assessment_details.title: Online Quiz Series
assessment_details.due_date: Module 1 quiz (15%) 17/08/2026 1:00 pm Module 2 quiz (10%) 31/08/2026 1:00 pm Module 3 quiz (10%) 14/09/2026 1:00 pm Each quiz will be available to complete for 4 days prior to the deadline.
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: There are three quizzes held during semester: ONE attempt is permitted for each quiz. The quiz questions include the content covered in UQ Extend and the practical class within the relevant module. See the Timetable and Assessment sections on Learn.UQ (Blackboard) for details of each quiz. Each quiz contain a mixture of question types, for example: multiple choice, multiple answer, matching, ordering, fill in the blank/s, jumbled sentence/s, either/or (e.g. true/false), short answer, and short essay style questions. Questions are derived randomly from a pool; therefore, each student may receive a different but equivalent quiz. The quiz will be marked electronically, and correct answers will be awarded the marks indicated beside the question; incorrect answers will be awarded zero. This is an individual assessment that you are required to undertake without any form of communication with other students. As an online quiz undertaken in the venue of your choice, the quiz is open book. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) technologies, successful completion of this assessment task will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which AI will provide only limited support and guidance. assessment_details.task_description: General information: This invigilated quiz will be completed in person at UQ Dutton Park during the scheduled workshop in Week 12. The quiz is paper-based with ONE attempt permitted. The quiz involves various pharmaceutical calculations, mostly related to compounding and dispensing liquid dosage forms, which you will practise in a series of practicals conducted regularly during the semester. The quiz duration is 40 minutes. Questions may be provided from a pool; therefore, each student may receive a different but equivalent quiz. The marks allocated to each question are provided on the paper; answers may be awarded zero, part-marks, or full marks as applicable to each question. This is an individual assessment that will be held under exam conditions. See Learn.UQ (Blackboard) and UQ Extend for more details, a sample/practice quiz, and marking criteria. Items that may be brought into the quiz: Your Student ID. Calculators must be Casio FX82 series or UQ approved (labelled). Pens: all answers must be written with an indelible pen, not a pencil and not an erasable pen. Mistakes must be neatly crossed through; do not use whiteout. Items that may NOT be brought into the quiz: Any other items, including any electronic devices. Materials that will be supplied: The question sheets (including space to provide answers). assessment_details.title: Compounding Skills Assessment
assessment_details.due_date: 27/10/2026 - 28/10/2026 School-based practical examination, held in the scheduled practical class at UQ Dutton Park in Week 13.
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment task is to be completed in person. Items that may be brought into the examination: Your Student ID. Laboratory coat, closed-in shoes and safety glasses are mandatory. Calculators must be Casio FX82 series or UQ approved (labelled). Australian Pharmaceutical Formulary (APF) - page tags are allowed, but annotations are not permitted. Pens: all answers must be written with an indelible pen, not a pencil and not an erasable pen. Mistakes must be neatly crossed through; do not use whiteout. Items that may NOT be brought into the examination: any other items, including any electronic devices. Materials that will be supplied: All ingredients and equipment required for the product that you will prepare and dispense, the prescription details, a compounding worksheet, and one copy of the current edition of the APF per laboratory. Instructions: You will have 90 minutes to complete the exam. You will work independently to prepare and dispense one assigned prescription. You will complete appropriate calculations, prepare the product, fill out the compounding worksheet, and label the product. Complete the compounding worksheet as you go. Ingredient weights and volumes entered into the compounding worksheet must match the value on the balance or in the measuring cylinder and must be checked by an invigilator. Raise your hand when you need an invigilator to check and sign against your entries. Prepare a suitable label and apply it to the product. To pass, your product must be of acceptable quality to be supplied to a patient. When you consider your product is ready to be supplied, submit the labelled product and compounding worksheet for assessment. Three components are marked, i.e. the product, the label, and the compounding worksheet. A passing grade is achieved when all three components are of acceptable quality for the medication to be dispensed to a patient. See Learn.UQ (Blackboard) and UQ Extend for more details, sample/practice exams, and the marking criteria. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.topic: Active online learning via UQ Extend The content for this course is delivered via UQ Extend. Each, week you should work through the active online learning on UQ Extend. You will get the most out of the weekly workshops if you have viewed the content on UQ Extend before attending the workshop. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

learning_activities.topic: Module 1 - Solid dose forms workshops One-hour weekly workshops held in person at UQ Dutton Park campus. Workshops will be recorded and recordings made available via Blackboard (Learn.UQ). Workshops will cover: Week 1) Solid dosage forms, tablets, and quality assessment, Week 2) Particles, powders and tablet formulation, Week 3) Drug dissolution from solid dosage forms. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05

Module 1 - Solid dose forms practical A three-hour practical in the laboratories at UQ Dutton Park campus. Working in a team, you will apply pharmaceutical tests to assess tablet quality. You are required to bring your own lab coat and safety glasses, and to wear closed-in shoes. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L05

Module 2 - Semi-solid dose forms practical A three-hour practical in the laboratories at UQ Dutton Park campus.
